rows.respond: Agree that the model isn't the difference. Ask how they'd know their own setup is right: incident.io says teams that build their own rarely measure accuracy, while it replays frozen past incidents and grades every hypothesis against what responders actually did.
rows.ask: The last time your agent named the wrong cause, how did you find out, and how long did it take?
rows.sendLabel: How they test it on frozen past incidents

rows.respond: Don't compete with their editor; join it. incident.io's plugin gives the coding agent they already use its skills, and Nexus can be queried from Claude or Cursor over MCP. What the editor doesn't do is start on its own: Investigations starts when an incident is declared, and can hold a page until it has a first hypothesis.
rows.ask: Who opens Claude Code at 3am, and how long after the page does it have the logs it needs?

rows.respond: Partly, and say so: anyone can call the same models. incident.io's case is the work around the model, which took it two years. The measured result: a median of 3 minutes from an incident opening to an accurate message in the channel, down from 6.7.
